title: Modified Andolfatto - Reduced Rep Sequencing
author: Jenn Coughlan
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bbjbikin
materials: Before you start: ·To order enough restriction enzyme for all of your samples. Calculate the total amount needed for all the samples that you plan to do, and order the appropriate amount of restriction enzyme. Ben Blackman did an in silico digest of the Mimulus genome and determined that Csp6I (G^TAC, not methylation sensitive)is a good enzyme to use, less frequent cutter, less cutting in repetitive regions that are difficult to map reads to. Order Csp6I, Fisher ER0211, 1,500 Units, 10U/ µL, ~300 digestion reactions per tube (or ~3 plates worth of samples). ·T4 DNA ligase may also need to be ordered. It goes bad quickly, especially if it is not kept consistently frozen, so buy more to be safe. NEB M0202M, 2,000,000Units/mL, 100,000 units. (50 µL per tube, calculate the number of tubes you need, 2 plates = 40 µL T4 ligase vol.) ·Carefully extracted genomic DNA that is not too sheared or degraded, these samples should also be quantified (using the Pico Green protocol if you have several plates or the Qbit if you are just doing a few samples. ·Phusion PCR mix may need to be ordered, check to make sure there is enough. You’ll need 25 µL per pool of samples. ·Check the amount of Agencourt AMPure PCR purification beads we have, order more if there isn’t enough. You’ll need ~225 µL of beads per pool of samples. (96 samples = 2 pools) ·You will need access to a UV table; a refrigerated centrifuge is also highly recommended
Anneal in thermocycler - hold the reaction at 95°C for two minutes, then cool to 30°C by lowering the temp 1°C per minute, then hold at 4°C.
Digest the DNA in a thermocycler for 3 hours at 37°C with a 20-minute incubation at 65°C at the end to inactivate the restriction enzyme

See *Annealing Adapters Section* to make adapters stock Master Mix: Amounts per sample Master Mix for 2 plates :5.0 µL T4 DNA Ligase Buffer (10X) 1000 µL T4 DNA Ligase Buffer (10X) 0.2 µL NEB T4 DNA ligase, LC 40 µL NEB T4 DNA ligase, LC 1.0 µL Unique Barcoded Adapter pair 1.0 µL Unique Barcoded Adapter pair (5 µM stock) (5 µM stock) 23.8 µL water 4760 µL water 30.0 µLTOTAL 5800 µLTOTAL
Ligate in a thermocycler for 3 hours at 16°C.

This part removes any leftover PCR reagents, enzymes, buffer salts, etc. The result from this step will be submitted for sequencing, so make sure to follow these steps carefully. Gently shake the bottle of AMPure beads to re-suspend them, make sure that no beads remain settled at the bottom. Shake them up just prior to pipetting because they will settle out quickly.

steps.title: Prepare Annealing Buffer
steps.instruction: Prepare the annealing buffer in a 50 mL conical tube.

substeps.instruction: Add 39.12 mL ultrapure water
Add 400 uL 1M Tris pH 7.5
Add 80 uL 0.5 EDTA
Add 400 uL 5M NaCl

steps.title: Prepare Barcoded Adaptor Pairs
steps.instruction: Prepare the adaptor pairs in 48 wells (half a plate or 8 strip tubes).

substeps.instruction: Pipette 95 uL of annealing buffer into each of the 48 wells
Pipette 5 uL of FC 1-1 and 5 uL of FC 1-2 into the first well
Repeat for remaining barcodes (FC 2-1/2-2 through 48-1/48-2)

steps.title: Dilute Genomic DNA
steps.instruction: Dilute genomic DNA samples to a standard concentration between 2–5 ng/µL (5 ng/µL is ideal).

steps.title: Prepare Digestion Master Mix
steps.instruction: Prepare the master mix for digestion. The following quantities are for 2 plates (total 3000 µL):

substeps.instruction: Add 400 µL Buffer B (10X)
Add 100 µL Csp6I (5U)
Add 2500 µL water

steps.title: Digest Genomic DNA
steps.instruction: Perform the DNA digestion in a new 96-well PCR plate.

substeps.instruction: Transfer 15 µL of the master mix into each well of a new 96-well PCR plate
Pipette 5 µL (10-25 ng) of diluted genomic DNA into each well

steps.title: Ligate Barcoded Adaptors
steps.instruction: Ligate the unique adaptor pairs to the digested DNA.

substeps.instruction: Transfer 29 µL of the master mix into each well of the digested DNA plate
Add 1 µL of the unique adaptor pair into each digested DNA sample

steps.title: Precipitate and Pool DNA
steps.instruction: Stop the ligation reaction and pool samples into 15 mL Falcon tubes (48 unique barcodes; each plate can condense to 2 pools).

substeps.instruction: Add 1/10 volume (5.0 µL) of 3M Sodium Acetate, pH 5.2 to each well (1,000 µL for 2 plates)
Add 1 volume (50 µL) of isopropanol to each well (10,000 µL for 2 plates)
Pool the reactions into 15 mL Falcon tubes
Incubate overnight at 4°C to precipitate DNA
Centrifuge for 30 minutes at 4°C
Carefully pour off the supernatant

steps.title: Wash and Dry DNA Pellet
steps.instruction: Wash the DNA pellet to remove contaminants.

substeps.instruction: Wash the sides of the Falcon tube with cold 70% Ethanol (stored at -20°C), ensuring the pellet is fully submerged
Centrifuge for 5 minutes at 4°C at the same speed as the previous spin
Carefully pour off the supernatant and remove remaining Ethanol using Kimwipes or a brief re-spin and pipette
Air dry the pellet until it is completely clear (not opaque)

steps.title: Re-suspend DNA
steps.instruction: Re-suspend the dried pellet in TE buffer.

substeps.instruction: Re-suspend the pellet in 100 µL TE pH 8 at 65°C for 30 minutes with intermittent vortexing (if difficult, incubate at RT or 4°C overnight or disrupt with pipette)
Move the entire volume to a 1.5 mL Eppie tube

steps.title: AMPure Bead Purification
steps.instruction: Clean the barcoded DNA using AMPure beads.

substeps.instruction: Bring AMPure beads and samples to room temperature (~45 min); shake beads to re-suspend
Add 1.5 volumes of beads (~150 µL) to the DNA and mix by pipetting up and down 10 times
Incubate at room temperature for 5 minutes
Place tubes in a magnetic rack for 10 minutes
Aspirate and discard the supernatant
Add 200 µL of 70% EtOH, incubate at RT for 1 minute, and discard supernatant
Add another 200 µL of 70% EtOH, incubate at RT for 1 minute, and discard supernatant
Remove as much ethanol as possible without disturbing the beads and air dry the samples
Remove tubes from magnet, add 22 µL of TE, and incubate at RT for 1 minute
Place tubes back on the magnet for 5 minutes
Transfer 20 µL of the supernatant to a new Eppie tube

steps.title: Gel Size Selection
steps.instruction: Perform size selection using a 2% agarose gel.

substeps.instruction: Add 6 µL loading dye to each sample
Prepare a 2% agarose gel: Mix 70 mL TAE buffer with 1.4 g Bio-Rad low range ultra-agarose and 7 µL Cyber Safe; use a thick/wide tooth comb
Place gel in rig and pour TAE buffer until just above the bottom of the gel
Load samples into wells, skipping a lane between each sample; load ~20 µL of Fermentas GeneRuler 50bp ladder into skipped lanes
Top off each well with TAE running buffer without exceeding capacity
Run the gel at 70V for 10 minutes to embed DNA
Fully submerge the gel in TAE and run at 70V for approximately 2 hours
Pre-weigh empty 1.5 or 5 mL Eppie tubes and record weights
Using a UV light table and a new blade for each sample, cut the band between 250bp and 300bp and place in the weighed tubes

steps.title: Recover and Quantify DNA
steps.instruction: Extract DNA from the gel and quantify.

substeps.instruction: Follow the QIAquick Gel Extraction kit protocol to recover DNA from each gel band
Quantify 2 µL of the column-cleaned DNA using a Qubit

steps.title: Index PCR Amplification
steps.instruction: Amplify targeted fragments and add indices using the Phusion PCR kit.

substeps.instruction: Set up a 50 µL PCR reaction: 25.0 µL Phusion mix, 2.5 µL FC1 (10 µM) INDEXED primer, 2.5 µL FC2 (10 µM) common primer, 2 ng template DNA, and water to volume
Run PCR program: 98°C for 30 sec; then cycle [98°C for 10 sec, 60°C for 15 sec, 72°C for 15 sec] for 14-18 cycles; final extension 72°C for 7 minutes; hold at 4°C

steps.title: Final Bead Cleanup
steps.instruction: Perform final purification of the PCR product.

substeps.instruction: Add 1.5 volumes of beads (~75 µL) and mix by pipetting up and down 10 times
Incubate at RT for 5 minutes
Place tubes in magnetic rack for 10 minutes
Aspirate and discard the supernatant
Add 200 µL of 70% EtOH, incubate at RT for 1 minute, and discard supernatant
Add another 200 µL of 70% EtOH, incubate at RT for 1 minute, and discard supernatant
Remove as much ethanol as possible and air dry for 5 minutes
Remove tubes from magnet, add 22 µL of Qiagen Buffer EB, and incubate at RT for 1 minute
Place tubes back in the magnetic rack for 5 minutes
Transfer the supernatant (~20 µL) to a new labeled tube and quantify yield via Qubit
